case.pattern_description: Under-threshold burst: 4 online purchases each between $450 and $499.99 ($1,906.07 in total) inside 30 minutes on a card with almost no online history, split across 2 New device profiles and 2 purchaser email domains. Amounts sit just under a $500 authorisation threshold. 12 other cards show the identical shape within 30 days (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06208-K1, C06881-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2); five closed cases with this shape were confirmed as undocumented fraud and reported.

case.summary: Verdict: fraud at probability 0.90. The pattern is an undocumented just-under-$500 online burst: four purchases of $478.95, $456.96, $488.04 and the flagged $482.12 (transactions 3476602, 3476633, 3476665, 3476682) placed within 30 minutes on 2016-11-21 across two new device profiles and two email domains, for total exposure $1,906.07. The decisive evidence was the customer's denial (customer family, floors probability at 0.55) combined with the graph-confirmed burst shape and the card's near-total in-person history — 255 of 261 transactions in-person versus only six online ever (history family); case memory of four same-device confirmed-fraud precedents (CC-5111, CC-3368, CC-3624, CC-1960) and 12 lookalike cards with the identical shape reinforced the read, against a lone legitimacy signal (low cms_p, memory family) that the floor overrides. No evidence request was needed or asked; recurring_charge_check was run and ruled out the R7 recurring-charge reading (only 1 matching prior charge, far short of the n≥5 gate), so the alternative "recurring pattern, not fraud" explanation does not hold here. The bank should create the case, block card C07297-K1 (L1, exposure ≤ $2,500), file a SAR (L2, exposure > $1,000 and undocumented coordinated pattern), and escalate to an analyst (auto) to review the 12 lookalike cards for the same burst shape. Stop reason: policy §6 test 1 fired — probability 0.90 is at or above the 0.85 fraud threshold with two independent evidence families (customer denial and card/burst history), and no further evidence request could change the action set, so the initial recommendation stands as final with nothing changed.

sar.narrative: This report is filed by the issuing bank regarding an undocumented coordinated fraud pattern identified on card C07297-K1 (debit, mastercard) held by customer C07297, tracked internally as case AC-HHG-006 (alert HHG-006), opened 2016-11-22. On 2016-11-21 at 20:00 UTC, an online purchase of $478.95 (product code C) posted to billing region 264.0 using device profile Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080, flagged as a new device, with purchaser email domain gmail.com. On 2016-11-21 at 20:10 UTC, an online purchase of $456.96 (product code C) posted to billing region 476.0 using device profile iOS Device | iOS 11.2.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2208x1242, also flagged new, with purchaser email domain yahoo.com. On 2016-11-21 at 20:24 UTC, a further online purchase of $488.04 (product code C) posted to billing region 476.0 on the same iOS device profile and yahoo.com email. On 2016-11-21 at 20:30 UTC, a fourth online purchase of $482.12 (product code C) posted to billing region 264.0 on the Trident device profile and gmail.com email; the customer disputed this transaction, stating she never made it. The four transactions total $1,906.07 and occurred within thirty minutes of one another, each amount sitting just under a $500 authorization threshold, split across two device profiles and two purchaser email domains. This activity is unusual for the cardholder, whose 261-transaction history since 2016-07-05 is overwhelmingly conducted in person (255 of 261 transactions) in billing region 264.0, with a median transaction amount of $58.98 and only six prior online transactions on two previously known devices; a same-day cluster of four online purchases near the $500 mark on newly flagged device profiles has no precedent on this account. Twelve other cards were found to show the identical under-threshold burst shape within the same thirty-day window, and five closed cases with this same shape have previously been confirmed as fraud and reported, indicating a coordinated pattern affecting multiple customers rather than activity isolated to this account. No prior SAR or case exists on this card, and OFAC/SDN screening returned no match for any subject. The bank opened case AC-HHG-006, blocked card C07297-K1, and is escalating the broader under-threshold burst pattern to an analyst for review across the twelve identified cards; this report documents total exposure of $1,906.07 across the four transactions described above.

stop_reason: Policy §6 test 1: fraud probability 0.90 is at or above 0.85 with 2 independent evidence families (customer, history); the customer-denial floor plus the confirmed under-threshold burst and case-memory precedents already settle the verdict, so no evidence request could change the action set and the initial recommendation is final.
